decision_reason: BunkerWeb is a current web-application firewall maintained and funded by the private French cybersecurity company Bunkerity: the project's own publiccode.yml names Bunkerity under fundedBy and its official company material identifies it as a private French company. The French SILL listing is a discovery/use listing, not evidence that an agency created, commissioned, funded or stewarded the product. I separately verified the public canonical source, the repository's AGPL-3.0-only grant, first confirmed licensed-source year, current installation documentation and named government-customer claims. No exact catalog duplicate found; no catalog entry added.

government_provenance.note: The product's own current publiccode.yml identifies Bunkerity alone in fundedBy and maintenance contacts. BunkerWeb's first-party About page says it is maintained by Bunkerity, a French company; no government product-origin relationship was found. The French SILL entry is not sponsorship evidence. The company page is https://docs.bunkerweb.io/latest/about/.

public_source.note: Public canonical repository contains the actual WAF/reverse-proxy code, tests, documentation and release assets; the repository is active and publicly downloadable.

eligible_license.note: The root grant is GNU Affero General Public License version 3, identified in the project's publiccode.yml as AGPL-3.0-only, an OSI-approved license for the first-party code in this repository. primary_evidence.note: Current first-party installation documentation installs the versioned 1.6.15 distribution. Bunkerity's BunkerWeb product page identifies Pau and Le Grand Périgueux as featured government-administration customers; this is a product-use/notability signal only and does not establish government origin.

decision_reason: ripgrep is Andrew Gallant's independently authored general-purpose command-line search tool, not a government-origin product. Its inclusion in the French SILL is a catalog/use lead and does not show agency creation, commissioning, funding or stewardship. The full public source, exact dual-license scope, earliest public grant and substantial independent integration into Microsoft VS Code were checked separately. No exact catalog duplicate found; no catalog entry added.

government_provenance.note: The first-party FAQ speaks in the author's first person about his licensing choices, and the initial public commit is in the individual maintainer's BurntSushi repository. No product-specific government commissioning, funding, sponsorship or stewardship evidence was found; the SILL listing is not origin evidence.

public_source.note: This is the actual public Rust command-line tool source, with tests, build instructions, user guide, release binaries and changelog; it is active and publicly downloadable.

eligible_license.note: The project FAQ and repository root offer a choice of MIT or The Unlicense for ripgrep; both license texts are present, and MIT is an OSI-approved grant for first-party project source. The FAQ says dependencies are also limited to permissive licenses; no government or public-domain status is inferred from authorship.

primary_evidence.note: Microsoft's first-party vscode-ripgrep repository explicitly states that the package is used by VS Code and packages upstream ripgrep binaries; Microsoft VS Code's own search documentation likewise says workspace text search uses ripgrep. This is documented independent software reuse. Current ripgrep docs and releases support a usable distribution.

product_identity: ripgrep (rg), a cross-platform command-line recursive regular-expression search utility
agency: No government-originating agency identified; independently authored by Andrew Gallant (BurntSushi). Microsoft VS Code is a documented independent downstream user.
geography: Project materials do not state a sponsoring-government geography or a specific product-origin location
license: MIT or The Unlicense at the user's choice for ripgrep first-party source; the project FAQ separately says its dependencies are permissively licensed
status_note: The initial public commit contains the root MIT and UNLICENSE grants and dates to 2016; repository metadata created_at is not used as a substitute for source-year evidence. Its strong independent adoption in VS Code is not government provenance. No exact GOSDIR catalog duplicate found.

decision_reason: Cachet is an independently created status-page product associated with James Brooks and Alt Three Services Limited, not a government-origin product. In addition, the assigned repository's current 3.x branch carries a bespoke Cachet license that restricts standalone distribution and is not an OSI-approved license; historical Cachet 2.x MIT terms and the separate MIT-licensed Cachet Core package do not grant the current application. Product docs, the GNOME production-use report and first licensed-source history were separately checked. No exact catalog duplicate found; no catalog entry added.

government_provenance.note: The first-party project identifies Alt Three Services Limited as the owner of Cachet's software copyright/trademarks; the original project license identifies James Brooks, and the official organization is a UK software company. No agency created, commissioned, funded or stewarded this product. SILL listing is not evidence of government provenance.

public_source.note: The current public 3.x branch contains the actual Cachet application source, tests and build files. Official user/install docs, a live demo and the versioned 2.x distribution are also publicly accessible.

eligible_license.note: The current app's custom Cachet license grants limited use/modification/bundling rights but prohibits distributing the software or modifications as a standalone product; this is not an OSI-approved grant. The old 2.4 branch has MIT terms and the separate cachethq/core repository is MIT, but neither MIT grant covers the current Cachet 3.x application repository.

primary_evidence.note: The official project recap reports that GNOME was already running Cachet 3.x in production; the first-party site also links current documentation and a live demo, and the project blog published a July 2026 development update. This is current product/use evidence, not government authorship or an eligible license.

decision_reason: The Chamber of Commerce of Romagna is the named software owner, and its first-party repository README says CISE, the Chamber's special agency, wholly developed the Java CMS and that the Chamber used it. The public code and AGPL-3.0-only first-party grant are verifiable. Hold because the source has had no commit since July 2022 (over 48 months), and current official evidence does not confirm that this exact repository still powers a live Chamber service: a 2022 Chamber specification describes a later institutional-portal redesign using the separate Open 2.0 framework. Confirm current product/source parity or continuing support before treating it as a current reusable product. The Developers Italia 2018 releaseDate is metadata, not the source year. No exact catalog duplicate found; no catalog entry added.

government_provenance.note: The repository under the Chamber of Commerce of Romagna's official GitHub organization states that the Chamber owns the software and that CISE (its special agency) entirely developed the product. The Chamber's public-administration identity is independently listed by Italy's IPA directory: https://www.indicepa.gov.it/ipa-portale/consultazione/responsabile-transizione-digitale/ricerca-responsabile-transizione-digitale/scheda-ente/1662.

public_source.note: The public repository includes first-party Java application source, database/build material, a source archive, installation/system requirements and a user/editor guide. The account profile links to the Chamber's official website.

eligible_license.note: The direct repository license text is GNU AGPL version 3; its publiccode.yml states the exact SPDX expression AGPL-3.0-only, an OSI-approved license for this first-party Java CMS source. The separately installed application server, database and Apache tools keep their own licenses.

primary_evidence.note: The first-party README gives user/installation details and says the software was used by the Chamber, establishing historical government use. However, the repository's latest commit is 2022-07-12, and no current official service/support record ties this exact source to the live portal. The Chamber's official 2022 procurement specification describes a portal rebranding using Open 2.0: https://servizi.romagna.camcom.it/download/amministrazione-trasparente/bandi-di-gara-e-contratti/atti-delle-amministrazioni-aggiudicatrici-e-degli-enti-aggiudicatori-distintamente-per-ogni-procedura/determinazioni-a-contrarre/determinazione-n129-del-28122022/determinazione-n129-del-28122022-allegato/determinazione-n129-del-28122022-allegato.pdf?DWN=13131. This creates a source-parity/current-use question, not a provenance or license failure.

decision_reason: caMicroscope is an NCI-sponsored digital pathology image-viewing/annotation platform with product-specific evidence in NCI's research-program report and NCI installation documentation. Its viewer source is public, and the full hosted distribution is linked by the project. The viewer (BSD-3-Clause), Caracal backend (GPL-3.0-only) and Distro deployment repository (BSD-3-Clause) have separate direct OSI-approved first-party grants; these are not extended to third-party services/dependencies. A peer-reviewed pathology study documents actual caMicroscope use, and the active project published version 3.13.0 in August 2026. All four checks, the exact scope boundaries and current-use/notability baseline pass. No exact catalog duplicate found; no catalog entry added.

government_provenance.note: The Leidos Biomedical Research report for the Frederick National Laboratory's NCI research program identifies caMicroscope by name as a digital-pathology subproject, describes NCI-funded precursor activities and its federally supported expansion. The official NCI Clinical and Translational Imaging Informatics project also published the product's deployment/install guide: https://wiki.nci.nih.gov/spaces/CTIIP/pages/325550279/caMicroscope%2BDeployment%2BInstallation%2BGuide. This establishes an NCI-specific commissioned/funded research relationship without claiming that NCI alone authored every component.

public_source.note: The assigned repo contains the actual public caMicroscope viewer application source, tests, user guide and build instructions. The project README identifies the public full hosted distribution in Distro and the separate Caracal backend; those public companion repos were also inspected.

eligible_license.note: The assigned viewer source has a direct BSD 3-Clause grant. The documented hosted distribution is multi-repository: Distro has its own BSD 3-Clause license (https://github.com/camicroscope/Distro/blob/master/LICENSE), and the Caracal backend has its own GNU GPL v3 grant (https://github.com/camicroscope/Caracal/blob/master/LICENSE). These are distinct OSI-approved grants for those first-party repositories; the Distro README names additional independent services, whose own licenses/notices are not covered by the viewer's BSD grant.

primary_evidence.note: This peer-reviewed pathologist-annotation study explicitly identifies caMicroscope as one of the two web platforms used to collect whole-slide image annotations for the study. Current operational documentation is available at https://github.com/camicroscope/caMicroscope/blob/master/README.md and the canonical repository published release v3.13.0 on 2026-08-19; the active 2026 source/release history satisfies the freshness baseline and the scholarly use satisfies notability.

product_identity: caMicroscope, a web-based biomedical image and data platform for cancer whole-slide pathology viewing, annotation and collaboration; the assigned repository is the viewer component of a documented multi-repository hosted distribution
agency: National Cancer Institute (NCI), NIH: product-specific NCI/Frederick research-program funding/commissioning; implementation involved Leidos Biomedical Research and academic collaborators
geography: United States (NCI/Frederick National Laboratory research program)
license: Mixed first-party grants by component: BSD-3-Clause (viewer and Distro deployment repository); GPL-3.0-only (Caracal backend). Third-party services and dependencies retain their own licenses; no repository grant is extended across component boundaries.
status_note: The root BSD-3-Clause grant was added to the viewer on 2019-01-25; older repository creation/development activity is not substituted for the first confirmed licensed-source year. NCI's 2016 install guide establishes prior federal deployment context, while the peer-reviewed study documents research use. Current repository activity/release v3.13.0 (2026-08-19), product docs and three separately checked first-party license scopes support publication. No exact GOSDIR catalog duplicate found.
